item.title: Josh Downs Describes How Chiefs Trade Went Down
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs caused a stir ahead of the NFL trade deadline . They made a move to land Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts to address their need at wide receiver. He described how the deal went down. Downs debuted for his new team in Week 10 versus the Atlanta Falcons. He finished with four receptions on five targets for 53 yards and one touchdown, showing that he is already building a strong connection with Patrick Mahomes. The star quarterback completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions. The Colts received a fourth- and fifth-round pick in exchange for the fourth-year wideout. Josh Downs entered the league as the No. 79 overall pick in the third round in 2023. He starred for the North Carolina Tar Heels in college, earning two first-team All-ACC honors. Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs (2) catches a pass during warmup s Sunday, Dec. 28, 2025, ahead of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Josh Downs Discusses His Trade To The Chiefs Josh Downs talked about when he found out he was headed to Kansas City. He highlighted that everything happened fast and how quickly his life changed. My whole life just changed in two-and-a-half hours,” Downs said. “I still got a house in Indy that I need to clear out and stuff. We didn’t really know what was going to happen at all. So it was like 3.30, 3.45-ish. I had texted my team pastor with the Colts and told him, I think I’m going to come to Bible study Wednesday night. I get a text from the Colts higher ups and they’re like, ‘Can you come see me?’ I was like, ‘Dang.’ And then I got a text from Patrick (Mahomes) then. I was like, ‘Oh, dang.’ Me and my dad were outside and I was like, ‘Dad, they just traded me to the Chiefs.’ “It was kind of like a buzzer-beater trade because it was like 3:50 at that time. It was kind of like a buzzer beater-trade because the trade deadline was in 10 minutes. So I had to go turn in all my stuff and then get on a plane like three hours later.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kansas City Chiefs (@chiefs) The move now allows Downs to be part of a legitimate Super Bowl contender with a chance to win the first title of his NFL career. Kansas City is currently 7-2 and at the top of the AFC West. The team entered the season with a chip on its shoulder, looking to prove that they should be one of the championship favorites. item.title: Dak Prescott Loses 3 Offensive Pieces as Cowboys Rule Out 5 Players for Week 11
item.description: Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns against the San Francisco 49ers last Sunday. Despite his stellar outing the Dallas Cowboys surrendered 584 total yards and could not escape a narrow 46-40 defeat. Now the veteran quarterback faces a sudden roster crunch ahead of Sunday’s home game against the Tennessee Titans. Friday’s final injury report revealed that Dallas ruled out five total players, including three key offensive pieces around Prescott. Dak Prescott faces sudden offensive shuffle after Cowboys rule out five players All five sidelined players missed every practice session this week before receiving their final game designations. On offense, Prescott will be without right guard Tyler Booker, tight end Jake Ferguson and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo due to lower-body injuries. Nov 23, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; A general view of a Dallas Cowboys helmet before the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Booker and cornerback DaRon Bland both suffered high ankle sprains during the loss to San Francisco. Booker started all 10 games this season and posted an impressive 83 Pro Football Focus grade that ranks fourth among all guards. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed concern after the 49ers loss about losing both starters, saying , “The two big ones I think will be Book with the ankle and Bland with the ankle. Both those guys are going to get X-rays, MRIs, and stuff like that. Both those guys could miss a little bit of time.” Ferguson remains sidelined with knee and ankle sprains suffered against Indianapolis in Week 9. He ranks third on the team with four touchdown catches and will miss his second straight contest. Mingo also sits out with an ankle injury. Cowboys Face Secondary Losses and Offensive Adjustments Against Titans The defensive backfield took an equal hit as Dallas lost Bland and safety P.J. Locke. Bland recorded 38 tackles and seven pass deflections across 10 games this year. Locke remains in concussion protocol after suffering a head injury late in the Nov. 8 win over Indianapolis. The Cowboys also listed safety Jalen Thompson and cornerback Devin Moore alongside tight end Luke Schoonmaker and linebacker Jaishawn Barham as questionable. Offensively, T.J. Bass will step in for Booker at right guard while Prescott continues to depend on top target George Pickens. Pickens recorded 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns against the 49ers. Prescott enters Week 11 with 2,724 passing yards and 21 touchdowns against six interceptions. Even with a shorthanded roster, Dallas opens as an 8.5-point favorite against a Titans unit surrendering a league-worst 266.9 passing yards per game. However, with the Cowboys ranking dead last in total defense at 393.8 yards allowed per contest, Sunday could turn into another high-scoring battle. Now the six-time Pro Bowler faces an unexpected challenge ahead of Sunday’s Week 11 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Friday’s final injury report revealed that the franchise ruled out three starting offensive players, including two key protectors on his line and his lead running back. item.title: Who is Evans Chuba? What to know about Purdue football starting QB
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − After 22 consecutive starts at quarterback with Ryan Browne , Purdue football went a different direction to begin Saturday's home finale against Wisconsin. Evans Chuba earned his first career start. It marked Chuba's fifth appearance as a Boilermaker . He came into the field late in the first half against Iowa on Nov. 14 on a third-and-1, his first snap in a still competitive game. Prior to Saturday's start, Chuba was 14-for-19 this season, throwing for 142 yards, including a touchdown against Notre Dame. Chuba played the first series against Wisconsin, throwing two incompletions on a three-and-out, before Browne checked in for the second series. More: Purdue-Wisconsin score today: Live updates as Boilers use two quarterbacks Here's what to know about Chuba, who has been Purdue's backup quarterback this season, his second with the Boilermakers . Evans Chuba is from Cananda with an eclectic breakfast palate Chuba grew up in Montreal, Quebec. Growing up, he did not like milk and had an affinity for mixing alternative drink choices with his cereal, he admitted this season during training camp. "With cereal, I put fruit punch, some days I even dabble with some 7Up, Sprite," Chuba said. "So you're eating the cereal and it's popping in your mouth." Chuba started his career elsewhere As a freshman in 2024, Chuba played at Washington State. He never saw the field for the Cougars and transferred to Purdue in the spring. Chuba did not see the field during the 2025 season at Purdue. Before this season, it had been awhile with in game reps Chuba attended Clearwater Academy in Florida, but missed his senior season with an injury. His first college playing time came in the 2026 season opener against Indiana State, when Chuba completed 4 of 5 passes for 29 yards. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. item.title: Thomason's heart typifies Wrexham - Parkinson
item.description: George Thomason has scored twice in his past three Wrexham appearances [John Mallett/ProSports/Shutterstock] Phil Parkinson says George Thomason possesses the key qualities Wrexham need in their squad following the midfielder's match-winner at Lincoln City. The 25-year-old robbed Daniel Oyegoke of possession before coolly slotting beyond George Wickens in the 82nd minute to earn the visitors a 1-0 victory over the Imps at ProAmpac Stadium. "He just typifies what we want here at Wrexham in terms of his heart, and he's a good player," Parkinson told BBC Radio Wales. Thomason started the contest at left wing-back but shifted to his preferred central midfield role after Ollie Rathbone was withdrawn through injury. And following his vital moment of quality late on, Parkinson praised Thomason for once again demonstrating his ability to operate in different roles. "Some of his link-up play was really good. Rathbone gets a dead leg, and we move him [Thomason] infield," Parkinson added. "He came to us as a midfield player; we converted him last year and he was probably close to getting player of the year in that position. "We need versatility and he showed that today." Thomason strike earns Wrexham victory at Lincoln EFL warns clubs over social media posts The win over Lincoln means Wrexham - who remain 14th in the Championship table - have claimed seven of the previous nine points on offer. They claimed victory without attacking talents Callum O'Hare, Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead and Sam Smith, who are all sidelined with injuries. However, the injury sustained by Rathbone at Lincoln does not appear to be serious, Parkinson went on to confirm. "It's just a dead leg. He tried to stay on; at first I thought it was his ankle, which worried me," the manager said of the 30-year-old midfielder. "It was a bang to his thigh. With the quality of Jacques [Ekomie] to come on and with Thommo to move infield, we had no need to risk him." Having withdrawn from Wales' squad to face Norway and Portugal in the Nations League due to injury, Kieffer Moore played the full match against Lincoln. But Parkinson was confident the 34-year-old would be available to feature against the Imps given the work the striker undertook during the international break. "It was more a problem with his back. We would never have risked him, but he had a full week in the international break of gym work and strengthening work," Parkinson said. "We've felt him into training gradually this week. "I think in games like that with his height in the middle of the goal, it's so important. "I was tempted to bring him off, and we wanted to try and win it with Cadz [Bailey Cadamarteri] at the top end of the pitch, but Kieffer's a colossus in defensive situations as well." The Twins, meanwhile, will try to keep Miller healthy, and see where best he fits. Seeing Lewis dealt prompted me to go back and look at the 2017 draft, and I think it is fair to say that the top of the first round has been a disappointment. Here’s how it shakes out: #1 — Royce Lewis, 4.9 bWAR. Unable to stay healthy, stopped hitting, traded. #2 — Hunter Greene, 12.8 bWAR. Traded to the White Sox prior to the 2022 season, non-tendered after the 2023 season, hasn’t signed with anyone since and is presumably out of baseball. #9 — Keston Huerta, 0.9 bWAR. Has a .203/.389/.381 slash line in 218 games with a -1.0 bWAR since. Spent 2026 playing for Kiwoom in Korea. #10 — Jo Adell, 1.3 bWAR. David Peterson, Tanner Houck and Brent Rooker highlight the rest of the first round, unless you count Drew Rasmussen, who was picked at #31 by the Rays but didn’t sign with them, presumably due to an elbow injury that necessitated Tommy John surgery a few months later. Ernie Clement is the only fourth rounder with a positive bWAR, and only three fourth round picks appeared in at least 30 games. Only one fifth round pick from 2017 has a positive bWAR. You may have heard of him. He was the Rangers’ closer this year.

item.title: 'Duty of care': Players' union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
item.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala (L) speaks to coach Vincent Kompany (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Global players' union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers' union said recent public comments made by Bayern's honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a "coordinated campaign" to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations". "A club of Bayern's standing should know better," the international union for professional football players said. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala... Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern's top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a "neurological disorder" which can lead to "temporary but treatable seizures". Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. "Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium," Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. "If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency -- because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable." Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. dwi/ea

item.title: Martin O'Neill's post-match reaction on CelticPlayer
item.description: Martin O'Neill's post-match reaction on CelticPlayer It may have been a frosty day in Glasgow’s East End today (Saturday, November 21) but Celtic turned the heat up on St Mirren , rushing to a three-goal lead by half time and adding a fourth early in the second half. The visitors pulled a goal back from the penalty spot but it wasn’t enough to halt the Hoops’ procession to another three points which, for the time being, puts them seven points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership table. Speaking to CelticPlayer after the match, Martin O’Neill gave his assessment on a good day’s work from the Bhoys. “I’m delighted.” The Manager said. “We played some really good stuff, particularly in the first half. “We had a really good lead at half time, we made a few substitutions during the second half, but overall I’m delighted with the performance and team. “It was a matter of being on the front foot early on in the game. Don’t be passive, be strong, be aggressive and I think we did all of that.” Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain opened the scoring with a finish following some good play from Yang, whilst Luke McCowan rounded off the first-half goals with a fine finish of his own. Martin O’Neill was keen to praise both men in his post-match reflections, telling CelticPlayer: “I’m really pleased for both of them. Absolutely delighted. “Alex has waited for his chance, and he’s a very fine player, a really terrific passer as well too. He took the goal magnificently. “Luke took his goal great, very well indeed. Sources cited in the report state that Roma are weighing up a move for the 26-year-old as they search for greater depth and quality in wide areas. The Serie A club are said to see Hudson-Odoi as one of a number of options, with the report explaining that he is “viewed as an alternative or secondary target behind Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens”, while “a loan with an option for summer is a doable deal”. Roma interest grows around Hudson-Odoi The background to that interest is clear enough. Hudson-Odoi “has found opportunities limited under Forest manager Oliver Glasner this season”, and the numbers outlined in the report underline that point. He “has made only five appearances for Forest this season, all from the bench, and has played only 45 minutes in the Premier League for the Tricky Trees”. For a player who has previously offered goals, assists and attacking thrust, that is a notable drop in involvement. Roma’s need is also specific. They are “seeking a left-sided attacking option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini” and appear to believe Hudson-Odoi could suit that requirement if circumstances align. Nottingham Forest stance on £10m deal Forest, however, are not under immediate pressure. Hudson-Odoi signed a new contract in August 2025, extending his stay until 2028, which leaves the club in a strong negotiating position. Antetokounmpo has been clear about the team’s current spot in the league. He told reporters that the Heat are not as bad as people say they are, but they are also not as good as people say they are. This middle ground is where the team must stay focused. The Greek star emphasized that keeping a steady mindset is key to survival. He urged his teammates to keep their heads down and build good habits daily. The Heat have a long road ahead with 67 games remaining. Coach Erik Spoelstra says the star forward is helping the team’s attack grow exponentially. The system works because Giannis moves without the ball and involves his teammates. item.title: Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Musiala comments
item.description: Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy [Getty Images] Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better". Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction". Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had" . The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested the deal may need to be renegotiated. "Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement. "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better." Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala? Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September. He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months". item.title: Three Victory to Keys: LSU vs. Tennessee
item.description: The LSU Tigers will look to end their losing skid in a tough environment today as they travel to Knoxville to take on #9 Tennessee. Here’s what the Purple and Gold have to accomplish if they want to win on the road today: Run The Ball: LSU has found success in the ground game in recent weeks, including a 45-yard touchdown run from Dilin Jones. However, the offensive playcalling has not allowed them to find a rhythm in the run game. Call the plays, run the ball, and don’t get discouraged if you only get a yard or two early on. Keep Playing Strong Defense : This season, the Tigers have played like a top 10 defense, and that was evident through most of the last two games where they held Alabama to 150 yards and 10 points through three quarters and then held Arch Manning and Texas to just 10 points before collapsing in the fourth. Keep your foot on the gas defensively, pressure whoever is at QB for the Vols, and don’t let it fall apart in the fourth. Play calling has gotten conservative, and it has almost felt like this team was playing not to lose, and it cost you two critical games. Even if you get out to a lead, continue doing what’s worked for you, take care of the football, and take the victory. The LSU Tigers and Tennessee Volunteers are set to do battle in Neyland Stadium in Knoxville at 2:30 p.m. CT on ABC.

item.title: The Lewis Moody message that inspired England to record win over New Zealand
item.description: England captain Maro Itoje revealed an inspirational speech from predecessor Lewis Moody inspired his side to a record win over New Zealand at Twickenham. Moody, a 2003 World Cup winner who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, joined Itoje and his side to stare down the All Blacks ’ haka in an emotional pre-match answer to the traditional Maori challenge. The 48-year-old had presented Steve Borthwick ’s squad with their match shirts on Friday evening and addressed the side, setting the tone for a 37-12 success – their largest over the All Blacks. “I got a call from [England’s Rugby Football Union chief executive] Bill Sweeney a couple of weeks ago and he got a message from Lewis' team about how we could potentially support Lewis on this game day,” Itoje explained. “Then the idea was floated about him potentially joining us for the haka and I took it away. I spoke to a lot of the senior guys in the team and there was overwhelming support to support Lewis. Lewis Moody joined England for a spell-binding pre-match display (Getty) “Lewis is such an inspirational man. He was an inspirational player and given his diagnosis the players jumped at the opportunity to support him. I think he and his family gave us that extra lift today. “”He came to spend some time with us yesterday. He presented us our shirt for today's game. He spoke to us, addressed us. There's no doubt that his presence, him joining us for the haka, him spending time with us gave us an extra lift. He was one of the guys I looked up to as a young boy playing rugby. I have the honour and privilege of captaining this great team, and to be able to welcome him onto the field is a memory that will live with me for the rest of my life. As an England group, we are so proud to be able to support him.” Moody was a try-scorer against New Zealand in 2002, the first of back-to-back victories over the All Blacks from a side that went on to win the World Cup. Itoje’s team have now emulated that first achievement having also beaten their opposition last November. The two teams could yet meet again on Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham. “The great thing about sport and the great thing about rugby is that it keeps presenting you with opportunities,” Itoje said. “We've had a good result today. We're very proud of our performance today but the great thing is that next week there's a new opportunity in front of us. “Whatever happens, we don't know exactly what's going to happen but whoever we play, whatever the circumstance, there's a new opportunity ahead of us and I guess we have the chance, we have the opportunity to take it.”

item.title: Walker Kessler flashes ‘f–k yeah’ moment in game of ‘f–k nos’
item.description: As Walker Kessler walked into the interview room, he uttered four words. “A win’s a win.” The Lakers, who have the NBA’s best record at 14-3, had eked past the Kings (1-14), who are in the league’s cellar. Walker Kessler (14) of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a 3-point basket against the Sacramento Kings on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images For Kessler, the Lakers’ 106-104 win on Friday was mostly forgettable. He got lit into by Lakers coach JJ Redick at halftime after only having six points and one rebound before turning things around to finish with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocked shots. He missed two free throws with 5.3 seconds left and the Lakers up, 106-104, a blemish that would’ve been much worse had Zach LaVine not missed his go-ahead 3-point attempt with 0.9 seconds left. But let’s focus on the positive. In a few days, no one is going to remember that the Lakers trailed the Kings by as much as 11 points in a game with 10 lead changes and 15 ties. All that anyone is going to remember is the W. Oh, and there was a major highlight. Kessler has already proven himself as an excellent rim defender and rebounder , but on Friday he revealed that there are some more tricks in his bag. With 11:42 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Lakers trailing the Kings, 84-82, Collin Sexton passed the ball to the 7-foot-1 center in the corner. Kessler then fired a 24-foot jumper which swished through the net. It was his first 3-pointer this season. So, you know, he’s shooting a stunning 100% from beyond the arc. Dylan Cardwell of the Sacramento Kings plays defense on Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It wasn’t exactly the play Redick called. He said it was “unorganized,” adding, “I’m not sure why [Kessler] was even in the corner.” But Redick loved it. “I didn’t bat an eye when he shot it,” Redick said. Redick then revealed why he was unfazed. During the preseason, after Redick drew an ATO that involved Kessler, the center wanted to make sure he did his due diligence by inquiring about all possible scenarios. Walker Kessler grabs a rebound during the NBA Cup game at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “We break the huddle and he’s like, ‘Coach, what do you want me to do if the ball finds me and we don’t get a layup on this play?’ Redick recalled Kessler asking. “And I said, ‘Shoot it.’ And he goes, ‘F–k yeah.'” So in a game with so many “F–k nos,” Kessler finally got his moment. “I feel good,” Kessler said, adding a caveat. “Should’ve made those free throws.”

item.title: Emegha And Lavia Get 7 | Chelsea Players Rated In Disappointing Loss Vs Leeds United
item.description: Emegha And Lavia Get 7 | Chelsea Players Rated In Disappointing Loss Vs Leeds United Chelsea welcomed Leeds United at Stamford Bridge earlier today as they hoped to secure a good result at home in the Premier League. The Blues made a decent start to the game and scored the opener in the 25th minute when Emmanuel Emegha found the back of the net. Noah Okafor equalised for Leeds just three minutes later as the two teams went into the half-time break with a 1-1 scoreline. Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored from the penalty spot in the 53rd minute before Okafor scored again just five minutes later. Brenden Aaronson scored another goal in injury time as the match ended with Xabi Alonso’s men suffering a disappointing 4-1 loss in front of their home fans. Let’s take a look at how each Chelsea player fared during the clash against the Whites. GK: Emiliano Martinez – 6/10 He made a few solid saves at the back but conceded four times this afternoon. RB: Josh Acheampong – 5.5/10 Acheampong did his fair share of defending but made a costly error at the back. CB: Wesley Fofana – 6.5/10 He made a lot of crucial clearances on the defensive end of the field. CB: Levi Colwill – 6/10 Colwill cleared his lines when he could and was strong in the air. (Photo by Jasper Wax/Getty Images) LB: Pep Chavarria – 6/10 He made two important clearances inside his half but failed to keep things solid defensively. CM: Romeo Lavia – 7/10 Lavia came back to defend when he could, but it was not enough today. He began the game well but had to be replaced in the 21st minute. RW: Estevao – 6.5/10 Estevao caught the eye at times on the right flank, but didn’t do enough to register a goal. CAM: Cole Palmer – 6/10 He managed to shine at times but failed to get his name on the scoresheet. LW: Morgan Rogers – 6.5/10 Rogers was a constant menace in the final third but gave away a cheap penalty. He has an assist to his name. ST: Emmanuel Emegha – 7/10 He took his goal well in the first half but was quiet in the second. CM: Jordan Henderson – 6/10 Henderson failed to impress during his time on the field. ST: Danny Welbeck – 6/10 He never looked like he would score. RM: Pedro Neto – 6/10 Neto made two decent chances in the final third. LW: Geovany Quenda – 6/10 He made one good chance up top.

item.title: Jorge Martin on keeping MotoGP title hopes alive: ‘I didn’t do anything, it was in Marquez’s hands’
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin admitted that he lacked speed in the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint, suggesting he owes his slim MotoGP title hopes entirely to Marc Marquez ’s crash. The factory Aprilia rider arrived at Portimao needing to outscore Marquez by 24 points over the weekend to take the championship fight to the Valencia finale. But after qualifying five places behind Marquez in seventh, Martin failed to make any headway in the sprint, gaining only one position in the opening 10 laps. That would have let Marquez seal the title with a third-place finish, but the Ducati star crashed out of the sprint on the penultimate tour as rain began to fall on the track. Speaking afterwards, Martin admitted that he was lagging behind the frontrunners at Portimao, particularly with his team-mate Marco Bezzecchi converting pole position into a dominant win. Asked whether he had kept his championship hopes alive, Martin insisted the outcome was never in his hands given the points situation. “Well, I didn't ‘keep’ anything. Everything was in Marc's hands,” he said. “For sure, it was a really tricky race. I didn't have the speed all weekend. Finally, in the race, it seemed I found a little bit extra. I was quite close to the podium fight, but I missed a bit more speed. “But in the end, I did my best. I finished in fifth position. Let's hope for a bigger improvement tomorrow. “When the conditions are really tricky like this, the focus more goes on riding because you need to be at 100%. “So you don't have room to think about anything. I was just really focused. I tried to fight the first few laps with Pedro [Acosta], trying to go in the front, and he was a bit faster. “We were catching the riders in front a bit, so this is good. I saw the places where I'm a bit slower, the places where I'm a bit faster than him.” Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Marquez has shown remarkable consistency since he returned from injury at the Italian Grand Prix in May, avoiding the kind of mistakes that have plagued Bezzecchi and Martin’s campaigns. The reigning world champion himself noted that his crash out of the sprint was his first real mistake in the second half of the season, coming just a day after he warned about the risks of racing with the title within reach. item.title: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win
item.description: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win Celtic’s midfield required some personnel changes this afternoon, with both Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur ruled out through injury. That presented an opportunity for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan, and they seized their chance to great effect, both of them getting on the scoresheet in the 4-1 victory over St Mirren and make a good contribution to the overall performance and result Indeed, Oxlade-Chamberlain, who opened the scoring just after the half-hour mark, was also given the Man of the Match award for his contribution. Both players spoke to CelticPlayer after the game, and the England internationalist said: “I thought in the first half we were pretty good,” he said. “We played some really nice stuff with the ball. “We defended pretty well throughout the half, and being clinical when you get the chances is massive. "Today we were able to do that. That obviously sets you up to be able to try and control the game a bit more. “In the second half, St Mirren played some really good stuff, to be fair to them, and had moments where they controlled it, but the lead that we gave ourselves in the first half made it a bit more comfortable from there.” And Luke McCowan was also delighted to play his part in the win over St Mirren, which saw him score Celtic’s third goal just before the break. He said: “It felt great. I worked hard to keep myself in the position almost, but I was just happy to be back out there playing. “As he (Alex) says, being clinical really helps. Obviously, in past situations here, we've probably not been as clinical, but today we were, and it helps us control the game." Fixtures Celtic Vs. St. Mirren - Sat, Nov 21st 2026, 15:00

item.title: UFC Qatar Highlights! Amir Albazi Scores Comeback Choke For First Win In Three Years
item.description: DOHA, QATAR - NOVEMBER 21: Amir Albazi of Iraq reacts after a submission victory against Alessandro Costa of Brazil in a flyweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at ABHA Arena on November 21, 2026 in Doha, Qatar. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) Amir Albazi re-entered the flyweight win column earlier today (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026) at UFC Qatar LIVE on Paramount+ from inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar, as the perennial contender ended Brazilian Alessandro Costa with a third-round submission (rear-naked choke). This fight was a tale of two rounds. Albazi dominated the first round by using his grappling and landing countless punches without answer. Costa is tough, though, so he was able to battle back in the second round and nearly finished Albazi with a barrage of strikes and a ton of takedowns. Albazi somehow survived, but the round was a massive momentum swing in favor of Costa. Albazi, who may have needed a finish in the third round to avoid a potential draw, let everything go in the final minutes of the fight. The Iraqi fighter was able to get the fight to the ground once again and found a way to get to Costa’s back. Albazi sunk in the tight rear-naked choke, forced Costa to tap, and walked off with his first win since a split-decision over Kai Kara-France back in June 2023. item.title: Nick Saban names his top national championship contenders, and Alabama isn’t one of them
item.description: Jul 22, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; former Alabama Crimson Tide coach and ESPN analyst for College GameDay Nick Saban broadcast during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images With just a couple of weeks left in the regular season, the College Football Playoff picture is starting to come into focus. And one of the most decorated coaches in the sport’s history thinks that only a few teams have what it takes to win it all. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban said on Friday that there are “three teams that have the right stuff” to win the national championship: Georgia, Utah, and Notre Dame. And despite spending more than two decades coaching in the SEC, he made sure to clarify that it was “no disrespect to Alabama.” Playoff Picture Taking Shape Georgia sits at No. 1 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings at 9-1, with its only loss coming against Auburn in October. The Bulldogs have won three straight since then, including a 48-21 win over Missouri last weekend. Utah is right behind at No. 2 and is one of two undefeated teams in the top five at 10-0, along with No. 4 UCLA, though the Utes needed a 40-39 win at Arizona last weekend to keep their perfect season alive. Notre Dame checks in at No. 6 at 9-1, with its only loss coming at BYU. The Fighting Irish have since won three straight, including a 31-24 win over Miami. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr were both named finalists for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award on Friday, according to On3. On the same show, Saban insisted that the SEC is still the best conference from top to bottom, despite the Big Ten winning three straight national titles. Yet only one of his three contenders plays in the SEC. ‘The right stuff’ Saban shared his picks during Friday’s appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . “I think there’s three teams that have the right stuff. And this is no disrespect to Alabama, because I think there’s probably seven to eight teams that can win the championship, Alabama being one of them. But if you’re a betting man and you say, ‘OK, who can run the ball, who can play good defense and who has a good quarterback?’ You would say Georgia has that, Utah has that, Notre Dame has that,” Saban said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Saban added that the rest of the contenders have weaknesses that could hold them back. “Everybody else maybe has a flaw somewhere along the way. Now they might be able to overcome it, but I think those three teams have the right stuff,” Saban said. That leaves out Alabama, which the committee has ranked No. 3, as well as No. 4 UCLA, No. 5 Texas, and No. 7 Miami, among others. Clearly, Saban thinks the national title race is a lot narrower than the rankings suggest. Although it is not guaranteed to happen, Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is on track to return for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions, per Tom Pelissero of NFL Network. Pelissero revealed why his return isn’t guaranteed yet, however. “Barring a setback, Baker Mayfield is good to go Sunday against the Lions. item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was a triumph of sorts. The hard numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the Sunderland box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable too. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the only survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic just seven months ago. With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving one of Zion Suzuki’s uprights with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka and comfortably eliminating the defender before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to a post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches. Continue reading...

item.title: Noah Okafor piles on pain for Alonso as rampant Leeds demolish dismal Chelsea
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty early in a one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that it was easy to conclude they would have won even without a helping hand from the officials. item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But when the momentum is against you, sometimes even a change of manager cannot stop the rot. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. Palace may feel themselves unlucky, but Thomas Frank started with a defeat and his side have now lost five successive league games. For much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour for a win that lifted them three points clear of the relegation zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
